questions.question: Explain the role of vitamin A and Vitamin D.
questions.solution_html:
• Role of Vitamin A and Vitamin D
  • Role of Vitamin A
  • l Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin essential for Vision,Growth and
  • Development,Maintenance of Epithelial Tissue,Immunity and Reproduction (1 mark)
  • l Vitamin A deficiency leads to impaired vision and damage to the eyes and also affects
  • growth,immunity and epithelial tissue health. (1 mark)
  • l Vitamin A deficiency results in eye problems,poor vision and increased risk of
  • infections.(1/ (2 mark)
  • Role of Vitamin D
  • l Vitamin D is a fat soluble vitamin essential for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus
  • from the intestine,which are vital for the growth and maintenance of healthy bones and
  • teeth. (1 mark)
  • l Vitamin D deficiency leads to impaired bone mineralization and other health problems.(1
  • mark)
  • l VDD causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.(1/ (2 mark)

questions.question: Explain the relationship between infections and Vitamin A deficiency.
questions.solution_html:
• Relationship between infections and Vitamin A Deficiency
  • l Vitamin A is called the Anti-infective vitamin.It is essential for maintaining a strong
  • immune system and protecting the body from infections. (1 mark)
  • l When the body lacks Vitamin A,the immune system becomes weak,and the protective
  • linings (epithelial tissues)of the eyes,lungs and intestines get damaged. (1 mark)
  • l In vitamin A deficient keratinised cells,the cilia of the epithelial cells are lost. (1 mark)
  • l This allows germs to enter the body more easily,increasing the risk of infections like
  • measles,diarrhoea and respiratory diseases. (1 mark)
  • l VAD also reduces the number and activity of white blood cells, maker it harder for the
  • body to fight infections. (1 mark)

questions.question: Explain the causes of hypothyroidism.
questions.solution_html:
• Causes of Hypothyroidism
  • l Iodine Deficiency-Lack of iodine reduces thyroid hormone synthesis
  • l Autoimmune thyroid disease(Hashimoto’s thyroiditis)-The body’s immune system
  • attacks the thyroid gland
  • l Thyroid surgery or radiation therapy-Reduces hormone production
  • l Congenital hypothyroidism-Present from birth due to defective or absent thyroid gland
  • l Certain medications-Such as Lithium and anti thyroid drugs
  • l Pituitary or hypothalamic disorders-Reduced TSH secretion leads to hypothyroidism
  • l Inflammation or infection of the thyroid gland. (Any 5 points, (1 mark) for each point)

questions.question: Describe the various consequences of undernutrition and the prevention methods.
questions.solution_html:
• Various consequences of under nutrition and the prevention methods
  • Consequences of under nutrition
  • l Delayed physical and mental development in children-slows down growth,resulting in
  • stunted height,underweight and delayed puberty.Affects brain development,leading to
  • poor cognitive function,learning difficulties and delayed speech and motor skills
  • l Reduced immunity,increasing risk of infections-Body more vulnerable to infections like
  • diarrhoea,pneumonia and tuberculosis
  • l Poor academic performance and productivity-Children suffer from fatigue,lack of
  • concentration and low energy levels.Adults -reduced physical strength and mental
  • alertness,decreasing work capacity and productivity.
  • l Increased maternal and infant mortality- Under nourised mothers-higher risk of
  • complications during pregnancy and child birth.Give birth to underweight or weak babies
  • who are more likely to die in infancy or suffer from developmental issues.
  • l Inter generational cycle of malnutrition- Under nutrition passes from one generation to
  • the next.Undernourished girls grow into undernourished women,who give birth to low
  • birth weight babies,continuing the cycle of under nutrition in future generations. (1 mark)
  • for each point)
  • Prevention Methods:
  • l Balanced diet rich in energy,protein,vitamins and minerals
  • l Exclusive breast feeding for the first 6 months and appropriate complementary
  • feeding afterward
  • l Nutrition Education and awareness programs
  • l Food fortification(iodized salt,fortified flour,milk etc)
  • l Micronutrient supplementation(iron,folic acid,vitamin A)
  • l Improved sanitation and safe drinking water
  • l Poverty reduction and food security programs-Govt.initiatives such as Public
  • Distribution System(PDS),Mid day Meal Scheme and Integrated Child Development
  • Services(ICDS) improve access to food and healthcare,reducing hunger and under
  • nutrition (Any 5 points, (1 mark) for each point)

questions.question: Explain the dietary management of Diabetes. [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the dietary management of diabetes
  • I Dietary Management:
  • A. Carbohydrate: Choose low GI foods, Increase fiber intake, Replace refined
  • cereals with whole grains
  • B. Protein intake: moderate protein
  • C. Fat intake: Prefers healthy fats (MUFA, PUFA) (3 marks)
  • II Meal Planning Techniques
  • • Plate method- Half plate- non starchy vegetables, One fourth- Whole grains or
  • millets, One fourth proteins, A small side fruit (low GI)
  • • Exchange lists: Food exchange lists
  • • Glycaemic load monitoring: Focus on both GI and portion size (3 marks)
  • III Foods to Include: vegetables, fruits, whole grains and millets, legumes and pulses,
  • low fat milk/curd, Healthy nuts like almonds and walnuts
  • Foods to Avoid: Sweets, desserts, chocolates, white rice, fried items, chips, samosa,
  • sweetened beverages, bakery foods containing trans fat (4 marks)
